Hi Emily — really helpful details, thanks. Quick read-through and an initial, high-level mapping below; we can iterate once Dev/Infra validate the KV/cache assumptions and you confirm typical sequence-length distributions (particularly how often you truly need 40k tokens vs. 16–24k).

Summary (first-pass):
- H100 (80GB) — best for sustained, large-context workloads. High memory headroom, strongest fp16/ampere performance for very large KV caches. Expect best P95 for long-context but highest unit cost.
- A100 (40/80GB) — good middle ground. A100-80 gives much of the H100 memory benefit at slightly lower perf on some kernels; A100-40 can be used for medium-length contexts but will limit single-request max context unless sharded.
- L4 (24GB-ish inference-optimized) — cost-efficient for short-context low-latency inference and quantized models. Lower memory means long-context work needs sharding or offloading; excellent for bursty traffic and cheap baseline capacity.

Preliminary recommended fleet mix (for discussion):
- Reserved H100 pool sized to cover ~60% of your long-context steady-state (to avoid expensive preemption and cross-shard overhead).
- A flexible L4 pool for short requests and bursty traffic (autoscaled).
- Small A100 fallback pool for large-batch/throughput handoff and to smooth transitional loads between H100 and L4.

Tradeoffs to confirm:
- If 75% of traffic really requires 20k+ tokens, H100 reservation needs to be larger (memory-bound) — cost goes up linearly with reserved H100 count.
- If you can apply aggressive KV/prefix caching and context window trimming, L4+sharding may be viable for part of the long-context mix, lowering cost but increasing engineering complexity and potential P95 variance.

Questions for you:
1) How many of the long-context requests can be served with a trimmed prefix vs. full 40k token context?
2) Any hard SLAs that must be met beyond the latency targets (penalties, uptime, region constraints)?
3) Procurement timing and preferred contract term (monthly vs. annual commit)?

If you like, I can run a quick capacity-sensitivity calc and a 3-month cost envelope for two scenarios (conservative: H100-heavy; cost-optimized: L4-first with H100 for anchors). Can we do a 30-minute call this week to lock the mutual action plan?

Best,

Tessa — that breakdown is exactly what we needed. Answers inline:

1) Trimming: ~40% of the long-context traffic could be served with a trimmed prefix (we can precompute condensed summaries for a portion of sessions). The remaining ~60% require near-full context (we decompress context client-side).
2) SLAs: No commercial penalties in the initial trial, but core product requires P95 < 700ms or we need fallback behavior to avoid user-visible timeouts. Region: US only for now.
3) Procurement: Preference is to close reserved capacity by end of July. Initial contract likely 6–12 months; we prefer to start monthly with a committed reserve afterward if the numbers look good.

Budget: we'd like a conservative cost target under $85k/month for the first 3 months if possible. Open to tradeoffs but want realistic ranges to present to finance this week.

Can you produce the two scenario envelopes you described and a short mutual action plan with milestones? We'll aim to finalize internal signoff by 7/22.

Thanks,
Emily
